name: add_requirement_match
description: Manually match an entry to an intelligence requirement (match_type 'manual'). Increments the requirement's match count and sets last_matched_at. Returns an error if the entry is already matched. Relevance: high, medium, or low.

name: add_tag
description: Tag an entry with an existing or new tag.

tag_name.description: Tag name (created if it does not exist)

name: add_telegram_feed
description: Subscribe to a Telegram channel feed. Requires server-side Telegram setup (scripts/telegram/telegram_login.py). The channel must be public OR the IntelFeed account must already be a member. Accepts @handle, t.me/https://t.me URLs (including /s/ preview URLs), or a numeric channel id. Invite links (+hash / joinchat) are rejected: join the channel first, then subscribe by handle or id. Queues an initial fetch on creation. Can optionally attribute every message to a threat actor or campaign. Use this for ransomware leak channels, hacktivist channels, and broker channels that are themselves the actor.

max_message_age_days.description: Skip messages older than N days on first fetch (0 = no limit)

fetch_interval_minutes.description: Minutes between polls (a lower value raises the risk of Telegram flood-wait limits)

threat_actor_id.description: Optional UUID. Every message is attributed to this actor

campaign_id.description: Optional UUID. Every message is linked to this campaign

session_name.description: Optional named session if running multiple Telegram identities

category.description: Category name to organize the feed under

name: add_to_campaign
description: Link an entry or entity to a campaign. Linking an entry or entity that is already linked returns already_linked instead of an error. The campaign UI and reports show names only for threat_actor, malware, cve, ttp and ransomware_victim links. Other entity types are stored but show as bare IDs in campaign views.

name: archive_intel_report
description: Archive an intel report. Its status becomes 'archived'. The report is kept, not deleted.

name: bookmark_entry
description: Set an entry's bookmarked flag for the current user (bookmarked=true by default; pass false to remove the bookmark). Syncs the flag to the search index. Returns the new value.

name: build_detection_summary
description: Detection engineering analysis of one or more entries. Gathers the intelligence linked to the entries and returns an attack chain analysis and the detection gaps. focus sets the angle of the analysis. include_existing controls whether existing detection rules are added to the context.

rule_formats.description: Rule formats to include in the summary

include_existing.description: Include existing detection rules for the entries' TTPs in the analysis context

name: bulk_entry_action
description: Apply one state action to a list of entries for the current user: read, unread, star, unstar, bookmark, unbookmark, or hide (hide also marks the entries read). Syncs state to the search index. Returns the count of entries actually changed.

action.description: State action to apply to every entry

name: bulk_unlink_entities
description: Remove up to 500 entry→entity autolinks in one call. Each item is {entity_type, entity_id, entry_id}. Items whose junction row no longer exists are skipped. Clears the cached pivots and graphs of each affected entity. Returns the number deleted.

name: check_detection_gaps
description: ATT&CK coverage analysis: observed TTPs compared with non-draft detection rules, with a summary per tactic and the list of uncovered techniques. Covers TTPs only, not CVEs.

name: check_requirement_match
description: Check an entry against all active intelligence requirements with the matching code the pipeline uses: linked-entity matches first, then keyword matches in the title and body, filtered by each requirement's min_relevance and feed filter. Read-only: stores nothing. Also returns the matches the pipeline already stored for this entry.

name: check_telemetry_feasibility
description: Check whether detection rules can run on the configured telemetry sources. Lists the log sources a rule needs and which of them are available.

rule_id.description: Optional: detection rule UUID to check

name: confirm_extraction_entities
description: Approve AI-created entities as an analyst: clears the needs_review flag on the given entities of one type, so they are no longer listed in the extraction review queue. Returns how many rows were updated.

name: confirm_relationship
description: Confirm a relationship as an analyst: sets source='analyst_confirmed' and confidence='confirmed', then clears the cached pivots and graphs of both entities. Returns the updated relationship.

name: convert_detection_rule
description: Convert a detection rule to a different rule language using the AI provider assigned to the detection_rules task. Target formats: aql, crowdstrike_ql, elastic_ql, kql, nuclei, panther, sigma, snort_suricata, splunk_spl, sql, sumo, yara, yaral. Returns the converted content without changing the source rule. With save=true, the conversion is stored on the rule's metadata under rule_conversions, where the UI also keeps saved conversions.

save.description: Save the conversion in the rule's metadata (rule_conversions).

name: create_automation_rule
description: Set up an automation rule with trigger, conditions, and actions. Trigger types: on_correlation_event, on_cve_detected, on_entry_scored, on_keyword_match, on_manual, on_new_entry, on_observable_captured, on_schedule. Each action is {type, config}; valid action types: add_tags, add_to_campaign, bookmark_entry, branch, chain_rule, create_intel_report, create_note, extract_cves, extract_malware, extract_threat_actors, extract_ttps, generate_detection_rules, hide_entry, mark_priority, mark_read, remove_tags, run_ai_task, run_webhook, send_email, send_notification, star_entry, track_on_threat_board, use_daily_summary. The rule is created enabled.

trigger_config.description: Trigger configuration (e.g. feed_ids, pattern, min_severity, execution_mode)

actions.description: Actions to execute, each {type: <action type>, config: {...}}

name: create_campaign
description: Create a new campaign to track a threat operation and link entities/entries to it. TLP markings use TLP 2.0 (TLP:CLEAR/GREEN/AMBER/AMBER+STRICT/RED); the legacy TLP:WHITE is accepted and normalized to TLP:CLEAR.

name: create_category
description: Create a feed category. Returns the existing category instead if one with the same name exists.

name: create_detection_rule
description: Save a detection rule to the library. The rule is stored as a draft (is_draft=true). An analyst promotes it from the Detection workbench. Optional provenance: tags, reference URLs, and the UUIDs of the source entries the rule was derived from.

references.description: Optional advisory/blog URLs the rule cites

source_entry_ids.description: Optional entry UUIDs the rule was derived from

name: create_entity_note
description: Add an analytical note to an intelligence entity. Supported entity types: campaign, country, cve, cwe, malware, mitigation, observable, product, sector, threat_actor, tool, ttp, vendor (matches the entity_notes DB constraint; ransomware victims are not supported).

name: create_feed
description: Subscribe to a new feed. feed_type covers every registered adapter (rss, atom, youtube, podcast, reddit, github_releases, github_advisories, github_repo, nvd, mastodon, web_scraper, telegram, bluesky). For telegram, prefer add_telegram_feed. Rejects duplicate URLs with a structured error and queues an initial fetch via Celery. Extended adapter types usually need an adapter_config (see the adapter's expected keys). If the named category does not exist, the feed is still created and a warning is returned.

title.description: Display title (defaults to the URL if omitted)

category.description: Category name to organize the feed under (must already exist)

name: create_glossary_term
description: Create a user glossary term. Requires name, category (free text; the NIST CSF functions govern, identify, protect, detect, respond and recover get their own colors), and description. Optional: maturity ('emerging', 'trending', or 'mature'), long_description, technologies (name + optional url), and search_terms aliases used for detection. Fails if a term with the same name already exists.

category.description: Category name, e.g. a NIST CSF function like 'detect'

search_terms.description: Alias phrases used when detecting the term in articles

name: create_intel_report
description: Create a draft intelligence report from a template with linked entities and entries. Templates with sections: actor_profile, campaign_tracker, detection_report, exposure_report, flash_alert, landscape_report; saved templates (ioc_bulletin, country_threat_brief, and any shared or your own) are accepted by slug. For a report you have already written, use template_type 'manual': it has no sections, and body holds the whole report as markdown. With another template, body is free text shown above the sections. Uses TLP 2.0 markings. The legacy TLP:WHITE is accepted and normalized to TLP:CLEAR.

template_type.description: Template slug, e.g. manual, flash_alert, detection_report

body.description: Markdown text. The whole report for template_type manual.

name: create_malware
description: Create a new malware family entity. Runs the entity resolver first: if the name or an alias matches an existing family, that entity is returned (created: false) and the new aliases are added to it. If the creation gates reject the name, the result is blocked: true with a reason. malware_type is mapped onto the controlled vocabulary. The raw value is kept in metadata.

malware_type.description: e.g. ransomware, backdoor, loader, RAT, wiper

name: create_note
description: Add an analyst note to an entry. Markdown content is rendered and stored as HTML (same as the notes API). If no title is given, one is derived from the first line of the content, falling back to the entry title.

title.description: Note title (derived from content/entry title if omitted)

name: create_report_share_link
description: Create a public (unauthenticated) share link for an intel report, or return this user's existing active one. The public page shows the rendered report (sections, data tables, tags) with no author or source ids. Only TLP:CLEAR and TLP:GREEN reports can be shared. AMBER and RED are refused, and a link stops working while its report has one of those markings. ttl_days sets an optional expiry on a new link. By default the API sets no expiry.

ttl_days.description: Optional days until the link expires (new links only)

name: create_requirement
description: Create a new Priority Intelligence Requirement (PIR).

description.description: What intelligence is needed and why

auto_match.description: Automatically match new articles to this requirement

name: create_saved_search
description: Create a saved search from a query-language string (e.g. "ransomware cve.severity:critical is:unread"). Saved searches are per-user and appear in the reader sidebar. display_name optionally sets a label to show instead of the name.

query.description: Search query-language string the saved search runs

name: create_share_link
description: Create a public (unauthenticated) share link for an entry, or return this user's existing active one. Share links belong to one user, so another user's link for the same entry is not reused. ttl_days optionally sets an expiry on a newly created link (the API default is no expiry). It is ignored when an active link already exists. When server-side TTS is enabled, the tool also tries to pre-generate read-aloud audio, which is deleted after 24 hours.

ttl_days.description: Optional days until the link expires (new links only)

name: create_threat_actor
description: Create a new threat actor entity. Runs the entity resolver first: if the name or an alias matches an existing actor, that entity is returned (created: false) and the new aliases are added to it. If the creation gates reject the name (tombstone, dictionary word, etc.), the result is blocked: true with a reason, and no entity is created.

name: create_webhook_preset
description: Create a webhook preset: a reusable URL, payload and header set. Automation rule actions can reference it by preset id instead of repeating the URL.

payload.description: Payload template as a JSON string (single-brace {var} placeholders)

name: decide_proposals
description: Apply a reviewed batch of Review-queue decisions in one call (POST /admin/hygiene/decisions). Each decision is {id: '<source>:<log_id>', decision: 'apply' | 'dismiss' | 'reclassify:<entity_type>'}. apply runs the row's own action. dismiss removes the row and the dismissal is kept: a dismissed reclassify covers the entity, and an adjudicator verdict is not filed again for its article. reclassify converts the entity and closes every proposal about it. The server handles duplicates: a row an earlier decision already closed returns 'settled', and an apply whose result already exists returns 'resolved'. Returns one result per decision plus counts. Admin only.

name: delete_automation_rule
description: Delete an automation rule permanently. REQUIRES user confirmation. The first call returns a confirmation prompt with a token. Show it to the user. Only call again with the confirmation_token after the user explicitly approves. To stop a rule from running without deleting it, use toggle_automation_rule instead.

rule_id.description: UUID of the automation rule to delete

confirmation_token.description: Confirmation token from a previous call. Only provide after user confirms.

name: delete_campaign
description: Delete a campaign and its links to entries, entities and saved searches. The linked entries and entities are NOT deleted. REQUIRES user confirmation. The first call returns a confirmation prompt with link counts. Show it to the user. Only call again with the confirmation_token after the user explicitly approves.

confirmation_token.description: Confirmation token from a previous call. Only provide after user confirms.

name: delete_detection_rule
description: Delete a detection rule permanently, with its version history. REQUIRES user confirmation. The first call returns a confirmation prompt and token: show it to the user, and only call again with confirmation_token after they explicitly approve.

confirmation_token.description: Token from a previous call. Only provide after the user confirms.

name: delete_entity
description: Delete a record: feed, entry, note, detection rule, campaign, automation rule, intelligence requirement, intel report, tag, or any intelligence entity (threat actor, malware, CVE, TTP, country, tool, vendor, product, mitigation, observable), by id or, for an intelligence entity, by name. Intelligence entities get the same cleanup as the API delete endpoints: entry links, entity relationships and pending Review proposals are removed and the search-index document is dropped. No tombstone is written, so the autolinker or extraction pipeline may create the entity again from future articles. Use the false-positive workflow if the name must not come back. For an observable, use the never-capture tombstone (deny_observable). REQUIRES user confirmation. The first call returns a confirmation prompt: show it to the user. Only call again with the confirmation_token after the user explicitly approves.

entity_id.description: UUID of the entity to delete

name.description: Instead of entity_id, for an intelligence entity: its name (or unique alias; a CVE id, ATT&CK technique id or observable value)

confirmation_token.description: Confirmation token from a previous call. Only provide after user confirms.

name: delete_entity_note
description: Permanently delete an entity note. The entity it was attached to is not affected.

note_id.description: UUID of the entity note to delete

name: delete_feed
description: Delete a feed for every user: it is removed from every feed list and is no longer fetched. Its entries are kept as the evidence behind entities, relationships, campaigns and story threads, but are hidden from the reader and default search. Adding the feed again restores it. REQUIRES user confirmation. The first call returns a confirmation prompt with an entry count. Show it to the user. Only call again with the confirmation_token after the user explicitly approves.

feed_id.description: UUID of the feed to delete

confirmation_token.description: Confirmation token from a previous call. Only provide after user confirms.

name: delete_glossary_term
description: Delete a user-created glossary term by UUID. Built-in system terms cannot be deleted. Deletes one row. No confirmation required.

name: delete_intel_report
description: Delete a draft intel report permanently. Published or archived reports cannot be deleted: archive them instead. REQUIRES user confirmation. The first call returns a confirmation prompt and token: show it to the user, and only call again with confirmation_token after they explicitly approve.

confirmation_token.description: Token from a previous call. Only provide after the user confirms.

name: delete_note
description: Delete an analyst note. The entry it was attached to (if any) is not affected.

note_id.description: UUID of the note to delete

name: delete_relationship
description: Permanently delete an entity↔entity relationship and clear the cached pivots and graphs of both entities. It can be created again, so no confirmation is required. For auto-extracted relationships, use reject_relationship instead: re-ingestion can create a deleted row again, but not a rejected one.

name: delete_requirement
description: Delete an intelligence requirement (PIR) permanently, with its entry matches. REQUIRES user confirmation. The first call returns a confirmation prompt and token: show it to the user, and only call again with confirmation_token after they explicitly approve.

confirmation_token.description: Token from a previous call. Only provide after the user confirms.

name: delete_saved_search
description: Delete one of this user's saved searches by id. The entries it matched are not changed, and the search can be recreated from its name and query.

name: delete_webhook_preset
description: Delete a webhook preset. Automation actions that reference it by id will no longer find it. Check which rules use it first.

preset_id.description: UUID of the webhook preset to delete

name: deny_observable
description: Admin: add a value to the never-capture list so it is never captured, sighted or exported again (a false positive, benign infrastructure, or a domain that belongs to an intel profile). Works on an existing observable by UUID or on any kind and value. Denying a value that is not in the observables list creates a tombstone row, so no capture path can add it later. Can be reversed through the API.

name: detect_glossary_terms
description: Detect which glossary terms appear in an entry's text (word-boundary matching over each term's name and search-term aliases). Returns matched terms with per-term match counts, highest first. Takes an entry UUID, not raw text, because the API only accepts an entry.

entry_id.description: Entry UUID whose text to scan

name: discover_telegram_channels
description: List every Telegram channel the IntelFeed bootstrap account has joined. is_subscribed says whether IntelFeed already ingests the channel. Use this to find channels joined in the Telegram client app that are not yet set up as IntelFeed feeds.

name: export_attack_layer
description: Export MITRE ATT&CK Navigator layer JSON for visualization. With entry_id, uses the entry's linked techniques with real tactic and per-link confidence/source text; without it, covers observed techniques (linked to at least one entry, non-deprecated, top 500 by article count).

entry_id.description: Optional: scope to TTPs from a specific entry

name: export_campaign
description: Export a complete campaign intel package: linked entries, every entity type extracted from those entries (TTPs, CVEs, actors, malware, tools, vendors, products, countries, mitigations), explicitly linked entities, and detection rules sourced from the campaign.

name: export_observables
description: Export a filtered set of observables as lines (EDL), CSV rows or JSON. Takes the same filters as search_observables, plus a minimum report count and a switch to include dual-use infrastructure. Values are returned refanged (usable form). Denied rows are always excluded, and infra-tagged rows are excluded by default.

name: export_report
description: Export an intelligence report in markdown or HTML format.

name: extract_cves
description: Extract CVE references from an entry and optionally enrich from NVD. Stores results.

name: extract_malware
description: Identify malware families in an entry with the entry_analysis AI task. May return the cached analysis from ingest instead of making a new AI call. Creates or links malware entities.

name: extract_threat_actors
description: Identify threat actors in an entry with the entry_analysis AI task. May return the cached analysis from ingest instead of making a new AI call. Creates or links threat actor entities.

name: extract_ttps
description: Extract MITRE ATT&CK techniques (TTPs) from an entry. Always runs regex matching. use_ai also runs the ttp_mapping AI task, whose result is cached per entry: a rerun reuses the current AIResult. Stores links.

name: fulfill_requirement
description: Mark an intelligence requirement fulfilled, optionally linking the intel report that fulfilled it (report_id).

report_id.description: Optional UUID of the fulfilling intel report

name: generate_campaign_report
description: Generate an intelligence report from a campaign's linked entries and entities. The report is created as a draft and AI generation is queued. Templates: actor_profile, campaign_tracker, detection_report, exposure_report, flash_alert, landscape_report (default campaign_tracker). Uses TLP 2.0 markings. The legacy TLP:WHITE is normalized to TLP:CLEAR.

name: generate_detection_rules
description: Generate detection rules from an entry's TTPs via the detection_rules AI task and store them as drafts. Supported formats: aql, crowdstrike_ql, elastic_ql, kql, nuclei, panther, sigma, snort_suricata, splunk_spl, sql, sumo, yara, yaral.

entry_id.description: Entry UUID to generate rules from

name: generate_full_report
description: Generate an intelligence report with AI from source entries. The report is created as a draft, then AI generation is queued via Celery. Templates: actor_profile, campaign_tracker, detection_report, exposure_report, flash_alert, landscape_report. Uses TLP 2.0 markings. The legacy TLP:WHITE is normalized to TLP:CLEAR.

focus.description: What the report should focus on

name: get_analytics
description: Get platform analytics: trending entities, intelligence velocity, detection coverage gaps, and overview stats.

entity_type.description: For trending: threat_actor, malware, cve, ttp

name: get_attack_layer
description: Get MITRE ATT&CK Navigator layer JSON for a specific entry's TTPs. Without entry_id, the layer covers all observed techniques: those linked to at least one entry, excluding deprecated catalog techniques.

entry_id.description: Optional: scope to TTPs from a specific entry

name: get_automation_logs
description: Get recent automation execution logs.

name: get_automation_rules
description: List automation rules with optional label filter.

name: get_automation_templates
description: List pre-built automation rule templates with categories.

name: get_campaign
description: Get campaign details with timeline, linked entries, linked entities, and detection gaps.

name: get_campaign_attack_layer
description: Get MITRE ATT&CK Navigator layer JSON for all TTPs linked to a campaign.

name: get_campaign_detection_gaps
description: Telemetry-aware detection coverage for a campaign's TTPs: covered, library_only (rules blocked by missing telemetry), and gaps (no rule).

name: get_campaign_timeline
description: Get chronological entries in a campaign, sorted by publication date.

name: get_campaigns
description: List campaigns with optional status filter.

name: get_correlation_events
description: Get recent correlation events: coverage gaps, trending entities, campaign and requirement matches, new TTPs/malware for known actors or malware, actor-malware co-occurrence, feed staleness/errors, exploit and CVE score changes, and KEV additions.

name: get_coverage_workspace
description: Detection coverage workspace for one threat (actor, malware, CVE or ATT&CK technique) over a window: its recent articles and the behaviours extracted from them, each with the quote it came from, the telemetry channels it needs and whether enabled telemetry can see it. A behaviour flagged below_line has no matching telemetry: a sourcing gap, not a detection gap.

entity_key.description: Entity UUID, CVE id or ATT&CK technique id

name: get_cve
description: Get CVE details including CVSS/EPSS scores, severity, CISA KEV status, GitHub PoC and Metasploit availability, structured NVD affected vendor/product links, NVD weakness (CWE) assignments, and linked article count.

cve_id.description: CVE UUID or CVE ID string (e.g. CVE-2024-1234)

name: get_cwe
description: Get a MITRE CWE weakness by ID, including its abstraction level (Pillar/Class/Base/Variant), parent and lineage, MITRE mapping guidance, catalog mitigations and detection methods, how many CVEs carry it directly and across its whole subtree, how many of those are in CISA KEV, and linked article count.

cwe_id.description: CWE UUID or catalog ID string (e.g. CWE-416)

name: get_daily_summary
description: Return the cached AI daily summary (briefing) for a day, or null if none has been generated. date is YYYY-MM-DD, defaulting to today (UTC). Read-only: this never generates a summary. Summaries are generated by the daily_summary AI task or an automation.

name: get_dashboard_stats
description: Get system-wide statistics: total entries, feeds, detection rules, counts for every entity type (ttp = observed techniques with linked articles; full catalog size in ttp_catalog_size), and recent activity (entries in the last 24h/7d).

name: get_detection_rule
description: Get one detection rule with its full content, provenance (source repo, author, license, references), draft or published status, whether the enabled telemetry sources can support it, and a syntax validation summary.

name: get_detection_rule_versions
description: List a detection rule's saved versions, newest first. A version is saved each time rule_content changes and before each rollback.

name: get_detection_rules
description: List detection rules. Optionally filter by rule type (aql, crowdstrike_ql, elastic_ql, kql, nuclei, panther, sigma, snort_suricata, splunk_spl, sql, sumo, yara, yaral).

name: get_documentation_page
description: Read one IntelFeed documentation page in full, as markdown. The slug is the path under docs/ without the .md suffix, e.g. 'architecture', 'user-guide' or 'diagrams/entry-pipeline'. Cite the page you used as a /documentation/<slug> link.

name: get_enrichment_data
description: Get enrichment results stored on an entity: CVE (EPSS, KEV, GitHub PoCs, Metasploit, NVD data), malware (Malpedia, Wikipedia), threat actor (Wikipedia), or TTP (Wikipedia).

name: get_entity_graph
description: Build a relationship graph centered on an entity. Edges are typed relationship records (verb, direction, confidence, provenance) at confirmed or reported confidence. Entities that only appear in the same articles are not connected. Co-occurrence data only adds proximity and evidence articles to edges.

window_days.description: Restrict the evidence window per node to N days

name: get_entity_infrastructure
description: Pivot from a threat actor, malware family, campaign or tool to its observables, in two tiers. 'claimed': attribution edges with evidence (uses, communicates_with, controls), each with a trust tier. 'reported_alongside': observables in articles that name the entity, excluding indicator-list files and newsletters. Answers 'what infrastructure does X use?'.

entity_id.description: Entity UUID (use the lookup tools to resolve a name)

name: get_entity_link_stats
description: Autolinking counts: entry→entity links by entity type and by source, the number of held matches (pending autolinks) waiting for their article's AI analysis, and the number of entity↔entity relationships that are not rejected.

name: get_entity_timeline
description: Get a chronological timeline of the articles an entity appeared in.

name: get_entity_whats_new
description: Latest developments for one entity: recent novelty and severity signals (first mention, new technique, new victim sector, exploitation news, ...) on articles linked to it. scoped=true keeps only signals whose subject is this entity, as the profile page does.

name: get_entry
description: Fetch a single RSS entry by ID with its content and all extracted intelligence: TTPs, CVEs, CWEs, threat actors, malware, tools, vendors, products, countries, and mitigations. The body comes back one window at a time, but the entities cover the whole article — when `truncated` is true, call again with `offset` set to `next_offset` to read the rest.

name: get_entry_graph
description: Get the relationship graph for all entities linked to one entry.

name: get_entry_insights
description: Get follow-up findings for one entry's TTPs, CVEs and threat actors: detection gaps (no active rule), campaign matches, intelligence requirement matches, and critical CVEs. Up to 10, sorted by severity.

name: get_entry_story
description: List earlier and follow-up articles linked to an entry by shared entities. Within 30 days before or after the entry, an entry is included if it shares at least one CVE, threat actor or malware, or any two entities of any type. Results are in date order, not ranked by relevance. For relevance ranking use get_similar_entries.

name: get_extraction_stats
description: Counts for AI-created entities (created_via='ai_extraction': threat actors, malware, tools, CVEs, TTPs): totals by type, the number that need review, are orphaned, are likely duplicates or were auto-confirmed, and how many were created in the requested window and in the window before it.

window.description: Creation window for the created_window / created_prev_window counters

name: get_feed_entries
description: List recent entries from a specific feed.

name: get_feed_value
description: Get feed value scores: a composite 0-100 score per feed for how much intelligence its entries contribute (entity yield, new entities, correlation events, detection rules, requirement matches).

name: get_feeds
description: List configured feeds of any registered adapter type (atom, bluesky, github_advisories, github_releases, github_repo, mastodon, nvd, podcast, reddit, rss, telegram, web_scraper, youtube) with health status.

name: get_hygiene_feed
description: Entity cleanup log in time order: the entity-link log and the entity-maintenance log merged into one shape (action, mode, applied, subject, reason, affected-entity links, origin). Filter by action code (comma-separated for several), log source, mode, origin (adjudicator = filed by the adjudicate stage, merge_review = the duplicate review, scan = the on-demand scans), pending only, or a since timestamp. Read-only. Proposals are applied or dismissed in the Proposals queue.

action.description: Filter by action code(s), comma-separated, e.g. 'needs_reclassification' or 'ttp_malformed_id,cve_malformed_id'

source.description: Restrict to one log source; omit for both

mode.description: shadow = proposals only, apply = actions that actually ran

origin.description: adjudicator = rows the adjudicate stage filed; merge_review = the duplicate review; scan = the on-demand scans

since.description: ISO timestamp; only rows created at or after it

name: get_hygiene_stats
description: Entity cleanup counts from both proposal logs: the adjudicate stage's mode and how many of its verdicts are not applied yet, pending reclassify suggestions and name, alias, vendor and id proposals, the orphan entity count, last run times, and how many actions were applied in the last 24h and 7d.

name: get_ingest_batch
description: Status of one ingest batch: per-item status (queued / parsing / created / expanded / duplicate / no_text / unsupported / too_large / failed), the entry id each item produced, and a summary. Poll until summary.status is 'complete'. Created entries then go through the pipeline and the one-pass AI analysis, like any entry fetched from a feed.

batch_id.description: Batch id from ingest_text / ingest_file / ingest_batch

name: get_intel_profile
description: One intel profile with its countries (resolved names), sectors (labels) and other scope fields.

name: get_intel_report
description: Get a single intel report including its full content (all sections, metadata, references).

name: get_malware
description: Get malware family profile with aliases, type, targeted sectors, associated actors, and the count of linked articles (article_count).

name: get_observable
description: Look up an observable (a row in the observables list) by UUID or by its value (IP, domain, URL, hash, cmdline, registry key, ...). Returns kind, role, current and base confidence with decay state, sighting count, how it was added (AI analysis, the adjudicator, a curated IOC list feed, a publisher's IOC table, a TTP observable, or an analyst) with the evidence sentence, first and last seen, and the most recent articles it was seen in. Defanged input (evil[.]com, hxxps://) is normalized.

observable.description: Observable UUID or the value itself (defanged ok)

kind.description: Optional kind to disambiguate a value lookup (ipv4, domain, sha256, cmdline, ...)

name: get_priority_queue
description: The analyst's reading queue, as the Priority Queue page shows it: unread entries that meet the radar threshold, ranked by signal score. Articles in the same story thread are grouped into one row, so a story covered by eleven outlets is one item, not eleven. Use this for 'what should I read next' or 'what is important right now'. Prefer it over get_triage_queue, which uses the older heuristic and does not group stories.

limit.description: Entries per page (1-200, default 25); thread rows are extra

unread_only.description: false also returns entries already read (default true)

with_threads.description: false turns off story thread grouping (default true)

cursor.description: next_cursor from a previous call, for the next page

name: get_profile_threat_surface
description: The threats to one intel profile: actors and malware active against its regions and verticals. Each has the evidence for the match (which region or sector, how many articles).

name: get_ransomware_disclosures
description: Ransomware leak-site victim disclosures (Leak Watch), newest first. Filters: group name, canonical sector slug, country (ISO code or name), posting age, substring search, and the user's watched victims and groups. sort is 'recent', 'group' or 'sector' (ties sorted newest first). Returns a paginated list. Empty when the ransomware tracker has not synced yet.

country.description: Filter by country ISO code or name

watched_only.description: Only disclosures that involve the user's watched victims or groups

since.description: Only postings newer than N days

q.description: Substring search on victim name/domain or raw group name

name: get_ransomware_group_victims
description: Paginated list of victim organizations disclosed by a ransomware group (a ThreatActor), newest activity first. Returns an empty page if the actor has no tracked disclosures.

actor_id.description: ThreatActor UUID of the ransomware group

name: get_ransomware_stats
description: Ransomware Landscape totals for the last N days: victim totals with week-over-week change, a weekly time series, top groups (with week-over-week trend), top sectors, top countries, and new disclosures that involve the user's watched groups, organizations and sectors. All zero when the ransomware tracker has not synced yet.

name: get_ransomware_victim
description: Fetch one ransomware victim organization by UUID: name, domain, aliases, sector, country, first and last seen, whether the user watches it, the groups that listed it, and every leak-site disclosure.

name: get_report_share_link
description: Return this user's active public share link for an intel report ({token, url, created_at, expires_at}), or null if they have not shared it. Other analysts' links are not returned.

report_id.description: Intel report UUID to look up

name: get_requirement_coverage
description: Get an intelligence requirements coverage summary: counts by status, priority and category, plus stale (active requirements with no match in 30 days).

name: get_requirements
description: Get intelligence requirements and their coverage status.

name: get_review_rows
description: The pending proposals behind one Review group (or every pending row matching the filters), newest first. Each row has its id ('<source>:<log_id>', what decide_proposals takes), action, subject, reason, payload, and `context`: the article text around the match, so the article does not need to be fetched. Admin only.

name: get_search_facets
description: Get available search facets: feed types (feed count per type), categories (feed count per category), and top tags (by entry usage). Use it to see what the system holds before searching.

name: get_sector
description: Get a sector's victimology profile: description and aliases, who targets it (found in articles, and explicit targets-sector claims), campaigns scoped to it, leak-site victim totals and top ransomware groups, victims by country, the intel profiles that include it, and recent articles.

sector.description: Sector UUID or canonical slug, e.g. 'healthcare' or 'financial-services'

name: get_share_link
description: Return this user's active public share link for an entry ({token, url, created_at, expires_at}), or null if they have not shared it. Other analysts' share links for the same entry are not returned.

name: get_similar_entries
description: Find entries similar to the given entry. When the entry has an embedding, uses the embedding index, which finds articles about the same story written in different words. Otherwise falls back to keyword search over the search index. Excludes the entry itself and its exact duplicates (same content hash).

limit.description: Maximum similar entries to return (1-30, default 10)

name: get_source_reliability
description: Get feeds ranked by intelligence contribution: entity extractions across every entity junction type, plus detection rules generated from each feed's entries.

name: get_stack_exposure
description: My Stack exposure board: every CVE that affects the vendors and products in the user's stack (watchlist mode='stack'). CVEs are ranked by exposure lift (KEV, EPSS and weaponization multipliers). Each has a detection state (defended, blind or no_rule) based on the configured telemetry sources. Also returns CVE counts per asset and counts for each urgency and detection state pair. Empty if the user has no vendors or products in their stack.

name: get_story_thread
description: Read one story thread. Returns its timeline (the spine field: one update per wave of coverage, saying what was first reported and what each later wave added), every member article with its role (origin, beat for an article that adds an update, or echo for a re-report grouped under another), the techniques, CVEs, products and detection rules found in the story, and the most similar threads. Open it in the UI at /priority-queue?thread=<slug>.

include_members.description: Include the full member article list (default true)

name: get_story_threads
description: List story threads. A story thread groups the articles that cover one developing story, with near-duplicate re-reports (echoes) grouped under it. Each row has its outlet count, article and echo counts, key entities, unread count, and the priority score of its highest-scoring unread article. Use this instead of searching for the same story many times.

status.description: open (still accepting articles), dormant, closed, or any. Default open.

name: get_telemetry_sources
description: List configured telemetry/log sources and their coverage. Useful for assessing detection feasibility.

name: get_temporal_clusters
description: Find entries that share entities within a time window. Useful for spotting emerging campaigns.

min_shared.description: Minimum shared entities to form a cluster

name: get_threat_actor
description: Get a threat actor profile including aliases, actor type, motivation, origin country, targeted sectors, associated TTPs, and the count of linked articles (article_count).

name: get_threat_board
description: The Threats board: actors, malware and exploited CVEs over a recency window, ranked by how many distinct stories mentioned them (not by raw article or outlet counts). Each row has its lead headline, the cached AI brief when present, source hosts, story and echo counts, the analyst's handled state, and the count of existing library rules (prior_rules). CVE rows also rank by an exposure multiplier (KEV, EPSS, weaponized) and carry their detection status (posture). Rows with is_story are story threads not linked to any entity. Use it for 'what is happening right now' and to choose what to research next.

facet.description: threats = actor/malware rows; vulns = CVE rows; all = both interleaved

name: get_trending_entities
description: Get top entities by mention count over a time window.

name: get_triage_queue
description: Get the priority-scored entry queue for analyst review, as GET /api/entries/triage returns it. Uses the signal-engine ranking when signal_engine_surface is enabled, otherwise the legacy composite heuristic.

name: get_ttp
description: Get a MITRE ATT&CK technique (TTP) by ID, including tactic, platforms, data sources, and linked articles.

ttp_id.description: TTP UUID or technique ID string (e.g. T1059.001)

name: ingest_batch
description: Ingest many URLs and texts in one batch under Manual Uploads. Each URL becomes one entry. A github.com/owner/repo link (optionally /tree/<branch>/<path>) is fetched once and becomes one entry per file, and no feed is created. Each text becomes one entry. Returns the batch id. Poll get_ingest_batch for per-item status (created / duplicate / no_text / unsupported / failed).

urls.description: http(s) URLs or GitHub repo links

texts.description: Texts to ingest, one entry each

is_ioc_list.description: Treat every item as a curated indicator list

name: ingest_file
description: Ingest one base64-encoded file (PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD, HTML, CSV, EML, ZIP, ...) as a manual entry. Stores the original under Manual Uploads, queues it, and returns the batch id to poll with get_ingest_batch. A .zip becomes one entry per file inside it. Keep files under the configured per-file limit (default 50 MB). The base64 payload must fit in one tool call.

is_ioc_list.description: Treat the body as a curated indicator list

name: ingest_text
description: Ingest pasted text (a report body, an advisory, a chat log, a list of indicators) as one manual entry. Stores the paste as a .txt original under Manual Uploads, queues it on the worker, and returns the batch id to poll with get_ingest_batch. Set is_ioc_list when the text is one indicator per line. It is then handled as a curated IOC list, so its indicators are added to the observables list instead of being held as candidates. Each paste becomes one entry.

source_url.description: Optional http(s) URL the text came from

is_ioc_list.description: Treat the body as a curated indicator list

name: ingest_url
description: Ingest a web page or article URL as a manual entry. Fetches and sanitizes the content, stores it under the Manual Uploads feed, runs the full intelligence pipeline (autolinking and extraction), indexes it for search, and broadcasts an ingest event. Optionally overrides the extracted title. Errors if the URL was already ingested.

url.description: http(s) URL of the article to ingest

title.description: Optional title override for the created entry

name: link_entities
description: Create an analyst relationship between two intelligence entities. The (source, verb, target) triple is checked against the relationship matrix and flipped automatically into its canonical direction (e.g. 'cve exploited-by actor' is stored as 'actor exploits cve'). Valid verbs (per-pair restrictions apply): attributed_to, communicates_with, controls, delivers, drops, exploits, exposes, operates_in, overlaps_with, related_to, subgroup_of, successor_of, targets, uses, variant_of. Written with source=analyst_created. If the triple already exists, it is promoted to analyst_created and its confidence, description and evidence are merged instead of returning an error.

evidence_entry_ids.description: Entry UUIDs that evidence this relationship

name: list_categories
description: List feed categories as a tree (top-level categories with nested children), each with its direct feed count.

name: list_documentation_pages
description: List every IntelFeed documentation page shipped with this deployment (slug, title, section, one-line summary). Start here when answering a question about how IntelFeed works, then fetch the relevant page with get_documentation_page.

name: list_entity_links
description: List entry→entity autolinks (junction rows) from all seven junction tables, newest first. Filters: entity_type, entity_id, entry_id, source (auto_link, ai, ai_reconcile, auto_extracted, manual), confidence (high, medium, low), a substring search on entity name or entry title, and a window in days. TTP and CVE links record no source, so they are excluded when source is set. CVE links have no confidence, so they are excluded when confidence is set.

entity_id.description: Only links pointing at this entity UUID

entry_id.description: Only links on this entry UUID

source.description: Source filter: auto_link, ai, ai_reconcile, auto_extracted, or manual

confidence.description: Link confidence filter: high, medium, or low

search.description: Case-insensitive substring on entity name or entry title

days.description: Only links extracted within the last N days (1-3650)

name: list_entity_notes
description: List the analytical notes attached to one intelligence entity, newest first, with author usernames. Supported entity types match the entity_notes constraint (ransomware victims are not supported).

entity_id.description: UUID of the entity whose notes to list

name: list_entity_relationships
description: All entity↔entity relationships where the given entity is the source or target, newest first, with the names of both entities. Each row has a verb (relationship_type), confidence (possible, probable or confirmed), source and evidence_entry_ids. Relationships an analyst rejected, and those below the configured minimum display confidence, are hidden unless include_rejected is set.

name: list_extraction_entities
description: List AI-created entities (created_via='ai_extraction') with a computed status: linked (in use), review (needs analyst approval), orphan (every article link removed, but its source article still exists), or dupe (a near-duplicate entity exists; duplicate_of names it). Filter by type, status, creation window, text search and source entry. Sorted and paginated. Each row includes created_confidence, needs_review, created_from_entry_id and the source entry title.

types.description: CSV of entity types to include (cve, malware, observable, threat_actor, tool, ttp); default all

window.description: Only entities first seen within this window

source_entry_id.description: Only entities created from this entry UUID

sort_by.description: Sort key: created (first seen), entries (article count), confidence, or name

name: list_glossary_terms
description: List security glossary terms alphabetically with optional filters: exact category (e.g. a NIST CSF function like 'detect'), case-insensitive name substring search, and built-in vs user-created (is_system). Each term has a maturity, descriptions, technologies, and search-term aliases.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring match on term names

is_system.description: true = built-in terms only, false = user-created terms only

name: list_intel_profiles
description: List the instance's intel profiles (named scopes such as a customer or portfolio: the regions, verticals and technology they care about), alphabetical. Use a profile id with get_profile_threat_surface to see which actors and malware target it.

name: list_intel_reports
description: List intel reports, most recently updated first, optionally filtered by status (draft, published, archived) or template_type slug. Rows include section names but not section content. Use get_intel_report for the full report.

name: list_notes
description: List analyst notes (entry-attached and standalone), pinned first then most recently updated. Optionally filter to one entry or search title/content by substring. Each note includes its author and, when attached to an entry, the entry and feed titles.

entry_id.description: Only notes attached to this entry UUID

search.description: Case-insensitive substring search over note title and markdown content

name: list_review_groups
description: The Engine › Review queue: every pending cleanup proposal from both logs, grouped into one row per entity, newest first unless `sort` says otherwise. Each group gives the entity, its proposal count, counts per kind (e.g. shadow_remove, adjudication_reclassify), proposed target types, merge targets, origin, the highest verdict confidence, the newest row's subject and reason, matched forms and a sample entry; `facets` counts proposals per domain and per origin. Read a group's rows with get_review_rows. Decide them with decide_proposals. `total` and `proposals` are the queue size. Admin only.

entity_type.description: Only groups about this entity type

sort.description: newest, count (most proposals first), oldest, or confidence (highest first)

name: list_saved_searches
description: List this user's saved searches with unread/total entry counts. Counts come from a 10-minute cache and are computed inline (via search-index queries) on a cache miss.

name: list_sectors
description: List the victim sectors (a fixed, seeded list of 21 industries) with counts per sector: linked articles, actors and malware with a claim that they target it, and leak-site victims in the last 90 days. Pass a slug from this list to get_sector, who_targets_sector, sector_victims or pivot_entity.

search.description: Match on name, slug or alias (e.g. 'banks')

name: list_tags
description: List every tag with its entry count, by name. The tag list is shared; the counts are the caller's view (their own assignments of a personal tag, everyone's of a global one).

name: list_telegram_feeds
description: List Telegram channel feeds with their adapter config: channel, last_seen_id, attribution, session, and error state.

name: list_watches
description: List the current user's entity watchlist rows with resolved display names. Each row has mode 'watch' (priority boost), 'mute' (hidden), or 'stack' (the user runs this vendor or product; used for My Stack exposure scoring).

name: list_webhook_presets
description: List saved webhook presets (reusable URL, payload and header sets for automation actions), ordered by name. Webhook URLs and header values are redacted. View them in the web UI if needed.

name: mark_all_read
description: Bulk-mark entries as read for the current user, optionally scoped to a single feed or a category. With no scope, marks EVERY entry in every feed as read, so confirm with the user before calling it without a scope. The search-index sync runs on a background worker. Returns the number of entries marked.

feed_id.description: Optional feed UUID to scope to

category_id.description: Optional category UUID to scope to

name: mark_entry_read
description: Mark an entry as read (read=true, the default) or unread (read=false) for the current user. Also syncs the flag to the search index and invalidates the feed unread-count cache.

read.description: true = mark read (default); false = mark unread

name: merge_entities
description: Merge duplicate entities of one type into a keeper, by name or id (POST /entities/{type}/merge): entry links move to the keeper, the merged names and aliases become keeper aliases, and the merged entities are deleted along with their pending Review proposals (a merge proposal into one of them moves to the keeper). Names match the entity name first, then a unique alias. Admin only.

keeper.description: The entity to keep: UUID or name

merge.description: Entities to merge into the keeper: UUIDs or names

name: merge_malware
description: Merge a duplicate malware family into another. Works like merge_threat_actors. Use mode='shadow' for a dry run. Always include 'reasoning'.

name: merge_products
description: Merge a duplicate product into another. Works like merge_vendors.

name: merge_threat_actors
description: Merge a duplicate threat actor into another. Moves all entries and country links from the source to the target, adds source.name and source.aliases to target.aliases, optionally updates the description, then deletes the source actor. Set mode='shadow' to log what would happen without making changes. Always supply 'reasoning' so the maintenance log can be audited.

source_id.description: Actor to merge away (deleted at the end).

new_description.description: Replace target description. Omit to leave existing.

reasoning.description: Why the actors are being merged. Recorded in the maintenance log.

name: merge_tools
description: Merge a duplicate tool into another. Works like merge_vendors.

name: merge_vendors
description: Merge a duplicate vendor into another. Works like merge_threat_actors: moves all entries, combines aliases, optionally replaces the description, then deletes the source. Always include reasoning.

name: pivot_entity
description: Find the entities related to a given entity because they appear in the same entries (one hop). Each related entity has a strength tier (weak, moderate or strong). Lists are ranked and paginated, and can be filtered by tier and by time window. related_counts gives the totals before pagination.

window_days.description: Only count evidence from the last N days

min_tier.description: Minimum strength tier. If omitted, the system default applies. Confirmed relationships are always included.

name: promote_observable
description: Add an observable as an analyst. Turns a staged candidate, or any value the article prints, into a row in the observables list with a sighting in that entry, a role and evidence. Use kind from: ipv4, ipv6, domain, url, uri_path, email, md5, sha1, sha256, ja3, ja4, cert_fingerprint, cmdline, path, registry, scheduled_task, service_name, mutex, named_pipe, user_agent, http_header. Defanged input is normalized. A value that fails the plausibility check for its kind is rejected with the reason.

entry_id.description: UUID of the entry the value appears in

role.description: c2, delivery, payload, phishing, exfil, exploit, scanning, persistence, execution, defense_evasion, credential_access, discovery, lateral_movement, collection

evidence.description: The sentence that presents the value as malicious

name: publish_report
description: Publish an intelligence report. Saves the current version and sets the status to published.

name: reclassify_entity
description: Move an entity from one type to another when it was filed under the wrong type. For example, a malware family that is a tool, or a product stored as a vendor. Supports malware / product / threat_actor / tool / vendor. If target_id is given, the source is merged into that existing entity in the target type. If it is omitted, a new entity is created in target_type by copying name/aliases/description, unless target_type already has an entity of the same name, which it is merged into. Name the source by source_id or source_name (and the target by target_id or target_name). Type-specific fields (motivation, malware_type, vendor_id, tool_type, etc.) are not copied. Set them afterwards with update_entity_profile. The source's pending Review proposals are closed. Use mode='shadow' to log without making changes. Always include reasoning.

source_name.description: Source entity name or alias, instead of source_id.

target_id.description: Optional: existing target entity to merge into. Omit to use the same-named target entity, or create a new one.

target_name.description: Optional: existing target entity by name or alias.

name: refresh_feed
description: Queue an immediate background fetch of a feed on a Celery worker (same as the refresh button in the UI). Returns as soon as the fetch task is queued. New entries appear when the worker finishes.

feed_id.description: UUID of the feed to refresh

name: reject_relationship
description: Reject a relationship as an analyst: sets source='analyst_rejected'. The row is kept, not deleted, so re-ingestion and the co-occurrence engine cannot create it again or add evidence to it. It is hidden from pivots, graphs and relationship lists. Clears the cached pivots and graphs of both entities.

name: remove_entity_aliases
description: Remove aliases from an entity, by entity name or id. Entries linked only through a removed alias are unlinked and the stored article count is recounted (the same path as editing aliases on the profile). Alias matching is case-insensitive. Admin only.

entity.description: UUID or name of the entity

name: remove_from_campaign
description: Unlink an entry or entity from a campaign (the reverse of add_to_campaign). Provide either entry_id, or entity_type and entity_id. Only the campaign link is deleted, not the entry or entity, so no confirmation is needed.

entity_type.description: Entity type to unlink (optional, requires entity_id)

name: remove_requirement_match
description: Remove a matched entry from an intelligence requirement and decrement its match count. The entry can be matched again, so no confirmation is needed.

entry_id.description: Entry UUID of the match to remove

name: report_false_positive
description: Report an entity the autolinker linked by mistake. Always writes a FalsePositiveRecord audit row. With source_entry_id set, unlinks the entity from that entry. scope='entry' does only that. scope='alias' also removes entity_value from the entity's aliases and unlinks every entry that matched only on it. The entity is kept and still matches on its other names. scope='global' instead blocks the matched name from matching any entity type and queues a vocabulary rebuild. Existing links on other entries are not removed.

entity_value.description: The matched name that was wrong (1-500 chars), e.g. 'Prometheus'

scope.description: 'entry' = unlink from one article only; 'alias' = also remove the name from this entity and unlink articles matched only on it; 'global' = block the name for every entity type

source_entry_id.description: Entry UUID to unlink the entity from (optional)

reason.description: Why this is a false positive (optional, for the audit row)

name: revoke_report_share_link
description: Deactivate this user's active public share link for an intel report so its URL stops working. Other analysts' links for the same report are not changed. After this, create_report_share_link creates a new link with a new token.

report_id.description: Intel report UUID whose link to revoke

name: revoke_share_link
description: Deactivate this user's active public share link for an entry so its public URL stops resolving. Share links other analysts created for the same entry are left alone. To share it again, call create_share_link, which issues a new link with a new token.

entry_id.description: Entry UUID whose share link to revoke

name: rollback_detection_rule
description: Restore a detection rule's content (and type) from a saved version, identified by its version number (see get_detection_rule_versions). The current content is saved as a new version first, so a rollback can itself be undone.

name: run_ai_task
description: Run a registered AI task against an entry (e.g. article_summary, threat_assessment, detection_rules, entry_analysis). Returns the current cached AIResult when one exists for this entry and task. Pass force=true to re-run and replace it. The 'cached' field says which happened.

task_name.description: AI task name (e.g. article_summary, threat_assessment, detection_rules)

entry_id.description: Entry UUID to run the task on

force.description: Re-run even if a cached result exists (marks the old result not current)

name: run_automation_rule
description: Execute an automation rule immediately, once per matching recent entry. Trigger-level filters (keyword pattern, CVE severity) and rule conditions are applied first. Only entries whose actions ran count as matched. WARNING: this executes the actions once PER ENTRY. Never use it to test batch or briefing rules: it creates one briefing per entry. Use test_automation_rule (dry run) or the rule's schedule instead.

hours.description: How many hours back to look for entries

name: search_documentation
description: Full-text search across all IntelFeed documentation, returning the pages that mention a term along with excerpts around each hit. Use this to find which page covers a topic, then read it with get_documentation_page.

query.description: Text to search for across the docs.

name: search_entities
description: Search all 13 intelligence entity types and the analyst notes stored on the instance. The types are TTPs, CVEs, CWEs (weaknesses), threat actors, malware, detection rules, tools, vendors, products, countries, mitigations, campaigns and intel reports. Returns matching entities with type and key details. Note results use type 'note' and carry note_source: 'note' for a note on an article or a standalone note, 'entity_note' for a note attached to an entity. Their description snippet is centred on the match, not the note's opening line.

name: search_entries
description: Full-text search across RSS entries. Returns titles, summaries, dates, and feed names. Supports the full query language: AND/OR/NOT, quoted phrases, entry fields (feed:, tag:, type:, date:, is:, media:, lang:, title:, author:), entity filters (threat_actor:APT29, malware:, cve:, ttp:, tool:, vendor:, product:, country:, campaign:, rule:), and sort:. Every filter is applied, not only the text terms. Supports pagination via offset for pulling large result sets.

query.description: Search query (text, boolean operators, field:value filters)

offset.description: Pagination offset for paging through large result sets (default 0)

name: search_observables
description: Search the observables list (IOCs confirmed by AI analysis, the adjudicator, curated IOC list feeds, publisher IOC tables, TTP host artifacts, or analyst promotion). Filter by substring, kind, role, lifecycle status, or how the row was added (captured_by). Sorted by last sighting.

query.description: Substring of the value or label (optional)

kind.description: ipv4, ipv6, domain, url, uri_path, email, md5, sha1, sha256, cmdline, path, registry, scheduled_task, service_name, mutex, named_pipe, user_agent, http_header, script, ...

role.description: c2, delivery, payload, phishing, exfil, exploit, scanning, persistence, execution, defense_evasion, credential_access, discovery, lateral_movement, collection

captured_by.description: How the row was added: ai_extraction (AI analysis), ttp_observable, ioc_list (curated IOC list feed), publisher_ioc (publisher's IOC table), adjudicator, manual (analyst)

infra_tag.description: Dual-use tag filter: a tag (vpn, proxy, tor, rmm, kvm, scanner, phish_sim, benign_service), 'any', or 'none' for untagged rows only

min_reports.description: Minimum report_count (the number of articles that reported it)

linked_entity_type.description: With linked_entity_id: only this entity's infrastructure (threat_actor, malware, campaign, tool)

linked_entity_id.description: UUID of the entity to restrict to

name: search_unified
description: Unified search across both entries and entities simultaneously, with the full query language (boolean operators, entry fields like feed:/tag:/date:, entity filters like threat_actor:APT29, sort:). Entity filters constrain entry results via linked entries. Returns combined results grouped by type.

query.description: Search query (text, boolean operators, field:value filters)

name: sector_victims
description: Leak-site ransomware victims in a sector: totals (all time and in the window), monthly counts for 12 months, the ransomware groups posting the most victims in that sector, victims by country and the most recent disclosures.

sector.description: Sector UUID or canonical slug, e.g. 'healthcare' or 'financial-services'

name: set_detection_rule_status
description: Set a detection rule's status to 'draft' or 'published'. This sets the API's is_draft flag. Detection rules have no other states.

name: set_target_sector
description: Add or remove an analyst claim that a threat actor or malware family targets a sector. The claim is stored on the target-sector junction, and the profile's sector chips are rebuilt from it. action='add' turns an existing rollup or enrichment claim into an analyst claim. action='remove' removes the claim. The nightly rollup adds it again if the entity's own articles still contain the evidence.

sector.description: Sector UUID or canonical slug, e.g. 'healthcare' or 'financial-services'

name: star_entry
description: Set an entry's starred flag for the current user (starred=true by default; pass false to unstar). Syncs the flag to the search index. Returns the new value.

name: suggest_campaign_entries
description: Suggest entries that share entities with a campaign but aren't yet linked to it.

name: test_automation_rule
description: Dry-run an automation rule against an entry to see what would happen without executing actions.

name: toggle_automation_rule
description: Switch an automation rule between enabled and disabled, and return the new state.

rule_id.description: UUID of the automation rule to toggle

name: translate_entry
description: Translate an entry's HTML content (and title) via the LibreTranslate sidecar and store the translation on the entry row. Re-requesting with the same target language returns the cached translation; a different target re-translates. target is an ISO-639-1 code and defaults to the configured target language (usually 'en').

target.description: Target ISO-639-1 language code (default from settings)

name: unlink_entity_from_entry
description: Remove one entry→entity autolink (junction row) and clear the entity's cached pivots and graphs. The autolinker or an analyst can create the link again, so no confirmation is required. Does not change the entity or the entry.

entry_id.description: UUID of the entry to unlink

name: unwatch_entity
description: Remove the current user's watch/mute/stack row on an entity. Can be undone by calling watch_entity again. No confirmation required.

name: update_automation_rule
description: Partially update an automation rule. Only the provided fields change (same as PUT /api/automation/rules/{id}). Trigger types: on_correlation_event, on_cve_detected, on_entry_scored, on_keyword_match, on_manual, on_new_entry, on_observable_captured, on_schedule. Each action is {type, config}; valid action types: add_tags, add_to_campaign, bookmark_entry, branch, chain_rule, create_intel_report, create_note, extract_cves, extract_malware, extract_threat_actors, extract_ttps, generate_detection_rules, hide_entry, mark_priority, mark_read, remove_tags, run_ai_task, run_webhook, send_email, send_notification, star_entry, track_on_threat_board, use_daily_summary (actions inside a branch are validated too). actions replaces the whole action list.

trigger_config.description: Trigger configuration (e.g. feed_ids, pattern, min_severity, execution_mode)

actions.description: The complete new action list. Each item is {type: <action type>, config: {...}}

name: update_campaign
description: Partially update a campaign. Only the provided fields change (same as PUT /api/campaigns/{id}). Statuses: active, monitoring, closed, historical. TLP markings use TLP 2.0. The legacy TLP:WHITE is accepted and stored as TLP:CLEAR. tags replaces the whole tag list.

name: update_detection_rule
description: Update fields of a detection rule. Updatable keys: title, description, rule_content, rule_type (aql, crowdstrike_ql, elastic_ql, kql, nuclei, panther, sigma, snort_suricata, splunk_spl, sql, sumo, yara, yaral), severity, tags, is_draft, log_sources, mitre_tactics, data_sources, notes, source_ttps, source_entries, source_actors, source_campaigns, metadata, change_description. Changing rule_content saves the previous content as a new version. A content or type change re-extracts rule metadata into fields that are not set (same as the API PUT).

updates.description: Fields to change. Unknown keys are rejected. UUID-list fields take string UUIDs.

name: update_entity_note
description: Update the content of an existing entity note. Other fields (title, type, tags) are unchanged.

note_id.description: UUID of the entity note to update

name: update_entity_profile
description: Update an entity's profile. Supports every profile type with per-type editable fields: threat_actor (name/aliases/description/mitre_id/country/motivation), malware (name/aliases/description/malpedia_url/malware_type), cve (description/severity/exploit_status/affected_products/exploit_availability), ttp (technique_name/tactic/description), country (name/iso_code/aliases/region/description), sector (aliases/description), tool (name/aliases/description/tool_type/malpedia_url/github_url), vendor (name/aliases/description/website/vendor_type), product (name/aliases/description/product_type/website/vendor_id), campaign (name/description/status/tags/tlp_marking). Renames are checked for name clashes. Removing aliases unlinks entries matched only through those aliases. New aliases queue a scan of existing entries. The search-index document is refreshed.

name: update_feed
description: Partially update a feed. Only the provided fields change (same as PUT /api/feeds/{id}). Changing the URL resets fetch state (etag, error counters) and rejects duplicates. category is resolved by name and must already exist. exclude_shorts only applies to YouTube feeds. adapter_config is merged into the existing config (Telegram channel URLs are normalized, Bluesky app passwords encrypted at rest). Setting any reliability, timeliness or relevance rating, or analyst notes, sets last_reviewed_at to now.

feed_id.description: UUID of the feed to update

url.description: New feed URL (resets fetch state; duplicates rejected)

category.description: Category name to move the feed into (must exist)

is_muted.description: Mute the feed (hides its entries from the main list)

retention_days.description: Entry retention window in days (0 or less clears the override)

visible_to_visitors.description: Show this feed and its articles in public read-only mode (never Manual Uploads)

adapter_config.description: Adapter-specific config keys to merge into the existing config

name: update_intel_report
description: Update fields of an intel report. Updatable keys: title, tlp_marking (TLP 2.0; legacy TLP:WHITE is normalized to TLP:CLEAR), status (draft, published, archived), content (full content dict including sections), summary, entry_ids, entity_ids, tags, change_description. Changing content saves the previous content as a version and increments the version number. Setting status to published sets published_at.

updates.description: Fields to change. Unknown keys are rejected. entry_ids take string UUIDs.

name: update_note
description: Update an analyst note's markdown content (and optionally its title). The stored HTML is re-rendered from the new markdown, same as the notes API.

note_id.description: UUID of the note to update

name: update_observable
description: Correct an observable: set or change its role, label or description, or pin its confidence so it stops decaying. Fields left out are not changed.

name: update_requirement
description: Update an existing intelligence requirement (keywords, status, priority, etc.).

updates.description: Fields to update: title, description, keywords, priority, status, category, auto_match

name: validate_detection_rule
description: Validate detection rule syntax. Returns validation errors, warnings, and suggestions. Supported formats: aql, crowdstrike_ql, elastic_ql, kql, nuclei, panther, sigma, snort_suricata, splunk_spl, sql, sumo, yara, yaral.

name: watch_entity
description: Create or update the current user's watch on an entity (upsert on entity type + id). mode 'watch' boosts the entity in priority scoring. 'mute' hides its entries. 'stack' marks a vendor or product the user runs (vendors and products only), and is used for My Stack exposure scoring. boost is the weight in priority scoring (0-5, default 1.0).

entity_type.description: Type of the entity to watch

entity_id.description: UUID of the entity to watch

name: who_targets_sector
description: Rank the threat actors and malware families that target a sector. 'reported' rows are ranked by how many articles describe both the actor or family and an attack on the sector. 'asserted' rows have an explicit targets-sector claim, with its source (rollup, enrichment, seed, analyst) and evidence count.

sector.description: Sector UUID or canonical slug, e.g. 'healthcare' or 'financial-services'
